description: Hi! I'm Samartha from Lalitpur, Nepal. For this challenge I want to make a top-down story game where you talk to forgotten Moon and Mars machines and collect their memory logs. Looking for storytellers, artists, and coders who love space and want to make learning fun for kids. Let's make the abandoned machines speak again!
summary:
Space Legacy is a top-down pixel-art game built in Defold where the player rebuilds an abandoned Earth outpost and reopens the route to the Moon.

As a Cadet under Commander Hayes, you explore Earth Base, collect Coins and Science, upgrade the base, and launch to the Moon. On the Moon you discover discarded Apollo equipment — Eagle, the Lunar Rover and more — and learn their real NASA history through a Field Journal, then return to Earth.

It addresses the Abandoned, Not Forgotten challenge by turning space debris and forgotten hardware into something players can find, learn from, and care about, instead of just reading about it. It is important because it makes NASA history playable and memorable, especially for students who learn best by exploring and interacting.
details:
What it does / How it works:

Space Legacy is a 2D top-down game. Player moves with WASD / Arrow keys, interacts with E, opens the Field Journal with J. HUD shows Coins and Science. On Earth, the player explores NASA buildings, solar fields and landing pads, collects resources and upgrades the base (Need 300 coins to upgrade). At the launch pad, the player chooses Moon - 500 Money + 300 Science - and watches the Launching to Moon... rocket transition. On the Moon, the player explores craters, finds Eagle and the Lunar Rover, reads real Apollo history in the Field Journal, and presses E at the return rocket to return to Earth.

Benefits / Impact:

It teaches real Apollo history through play, not a textbook. Players remember Apollo 11 (July 20, 1969, 21.55 kg collected) and Apollo 15 Lunar Rover (July 30, 1971, drove 27.9 km, collected 77.31 kg) because they find them in the game. It also raises awareness that discarded equipment on the Moon is history worth preserving, not just debris.

Tools:

Defold 1.14.0, Lua, HTML5 / WASM export, itch.io for hosting, Google Drive for demo slides.

Creativity:

Storybook-style HUD, Field Journal with real NASA data, Earth -> Moon -> Return loop, and Commander Hayes briefing that frames the whole game as Abandoned, Not Forgotten.

Factors considered:

Playability in browser, simple controls for non-gamers, accurate NASA facts, and clear SI disclosure below.

SI Disclosure:

AI was used for debugging help, pixel-art generation for backgrounds / sprites / rocket art, and drafting story and dialogue text. All game logic, level design, NASA data checking, and final edits were done by my team. NASA logo shown is NASA's official insignia used for educational identification, not SI-generated.
